feedback:
Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: Unknown canonical benchmark IRI(s): https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#I2_031_KiloNewtonQuantityShape, https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#I2_031_LoadCaseShape, https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#I2_031_ShipShape, https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#I2_031_StructuralMemberShape
Semantic validator feedback: Repair the deterministic vocabulary failure by removing the invented canonical I2_031_*Shape IRIs and using blank-node shapes or a non-canonical shape namespace. Also make the semantic encoding faithful: do not require loadPatchOrientation for every load case; require the controlled loadPatchHeightParallelToFrame orientation only for bottom structural members, while preserving the applicable side-member condition and transverse-frame applicability. Add the required transverseFrameOrientation check for side structural members if it is part of the verified requirement representation. Replace ABS in the SPARQL constraint with evaluator-supported arithmetic/comparison logic, retaining the <= demand-versus-strength check and tolerance scaled from the expected midspanPlasticCollapseLoad value.

Repair the derived-value tolerance check so it handles every possible expected midspanPlasticCollapseLoad value, not only exactly zero or positive values. The current SPARQL has no mismatch branch when ?midspanValue < 0, allowing an arbitrarily different plasticStrength to pass. Use evaluator-supported arithmetic/comparison branches with tolerance scaled from the expected formula result (and an absolute fallback near zero), while retaining the demand <= plasticStrength comparison and the existing bottom-only orientation applicability.

Repair the applicability and existence logic. Add sh:minCount 1 for nltl:hasStructuralMemberLoadCase on each applicable structural member (or the shared member shape); otherwise a bottom or side member with no load case can pass vacuously despite the required demand comparison. Keep loadPatchOrientation required only for bottom load cases and transverseFrameOrientation=true only for side members. Also do not impose KiloN on nltl:combinedShearAndBendingDemand unless a canonical unit declaration or explicit verified unit obligation is supplied; its canonical metadata declares no recommended unit, so the current unit restriction is guessed. Preserve the demand <= plasticStrength comparison and the tolerance scaled from the expected midspanPlasticCollapseLoad.
